verdicts.summary: Lean has a weaker form of it. The first identity is stated exactly: core_radial_reynolds is q^(-A) · ℓ_r = q^(-h) with A = 1/2 + h and ℓ_r = q^(1/2) built into coreVelocity and radialLength. Two things of the display are missing. (i) The arrow is not part of that theorem, which is a bare equality; it follows in one step from negative_power_tendsto_atTop with A := h > 0, so this part is packaging. (ii) The second assertion, Re_r = |u_r^(0)| ℓ_r = O(1), was not found: the identifier `reynolds` occurs in the whole declaration index only inside Scaling.lean, whose only core Reynolds theorems are core_radial_reynolds and core_axial_reynolds (coreVelocity × axialLength = q^(-2h)), and the latter is a different quantity — the core velocity scale against the axial length, not the radial velocity against the radial length. No declaration giving a scale for |u_r^(0)| was found.
